section: Post-independence consolidation - land reforms, tribal and border policy, national integration

accepted.s: Bhoodan Movement was begun by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at which place on 18 April 1951?
accepted.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan Movement at Pochampalli on 18 April 1951.
accepted.tq: Combine the founder, date and place to identify the initiating event.
accepted.sec: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the time of the beginning of the Bhoodan Movement, Pochampalli was situated in which administrative unit?
accepted.x: Pochampalli was in Nalgonda district of the then Hyderabad State; it is now in Telangana.
accepted.tq: Use the historical administrative setting rather than the present-day location.
accepted.sec: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first donor in the Bhoodan Movement, and how much land did he donate?
accepted.x: Vedire Ramachandra Reddy was the first donor and donated 100 acres of land.
accepted.tq: Match the individual with the precise quantitative detail.
accepted.sec: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gramdan represented which subsequent stage of the Bhoodan Movement?
o: Transfer of surplus land only to government employees
A whole village being gifted to the community
Abolition of all tenancy rights by the State
accepted.x: Gramdan was the next stage of Bhoodan in which an entire village was gifted to the community.
accepted.tq: Apply the distinction between individual land donation and community donation.
accepted.sec: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first Gramdan village, established in 1952, was:
accepted.x: Mangroth in Hamirpur district of Uttar Pradesh was the first Gramdan village in 1952.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first Bhoodan village and the first Gramdan village.
accepted.sec: Bhoodan and Gramdan - founder, village and state of origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Goa, Daman and Diu — Operation Vijay
2. Dadra and Nagar Haveli — Operation Vijay
3. Pondicherry — French enclave
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay, while Pondicherry was a French enclave. Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed separately in 1954.
accepted.tq: Separate the Portuguese integration operation from the French and separately liberated enclaves.
accepted.sec: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed in 1954 and subsequently made a Union Territory by which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Tenth Amendment Act of 1961 made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Match the territory with the correct Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.sec: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pondicherry was transferred de facto to India on:
accepted.x: The de facto transfer of Pondicherry took place on 1 November 1954.
accepted.tq: Use the exact transfer date rather than the later constitutional status date.
accepted.sec: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pondicherry was made a Union Territory under the:
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Amendment Act of 1962 made Pondicherry a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Identify the amendment by linking it to the French enclave concerned.
accepted.sec: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Goa acquired full statehood in:
accepted.x: Goa became a full-fledged State in 1987 after having been a Union Territory.
accepted.tq: Distinguish liberation, Union Territory status and later statehood.
accepted.sec: Integration of Portuguese and French enclaves  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which law abolished zamindari in the Andhra area?
o: AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act
AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation
Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
accepted.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act abolished zamindari in the Andhra area.
accepted.tq: Match the land-reform law with its specific institutional target.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in 1949 to abolish intermediaries in Telangana.
accepted.tq: Use the adjacent-year distinction among the early Hyderabad and Andhra land laws.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following laws was enacted in 1950?
o: Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act
Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
accepted.x: The Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act was enacted in 1950.
accepted.tq: Identify the law from its year among closely related land-reform enactments.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the:
accepted.x: The AP Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the Subba Rao Committee.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with the legislation it influenced.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956:
1. It required lease deeds to be written.
2. It prescribed a lease period of at least six years.
3. It came into force in 1961.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act required written lease deeds, prescribed leases of at least six years and came into force in 1961.
accepted.tq: Test several connected statutory features together.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 was primarily enacted in the context of:
accepted.x: The Telangana tenancy law was passed in the context of the Telangana armed struggle of 1946–51.
accepted.tq: Link legislation to the regional political and social circumstance that prompted it.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Telangana tenancy law, six years of cultivation qualified a tenant for the status of a:
accepted.x: A tenant with six years of cultivation became a protected tenant and acquired hereditary rights.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal consequence of the specified cultivation period.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Telangana tenancy law, a tenant could purchase ownership at 60 per cent of the market price in:
accepted.x: The tenant could purchase ownership at 60 per cent of the market price in 20 instalments.
accepted.tq: Pair the percentage with the corresponding number of instalments.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: By 1964–68, ownership under the Telangana tenancy reform had been acquired over approximately:
accepted.x: Ownership had been acquired over 85,409 acres during 1964–68.
accepted.tq: Retain the precise area figure associated with implementation of the tenancy reform.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1961 was considered weak mainly because of:
o: Absence of any ceiling provisions and lack of exemptions
Its exclusive application to forest land
Compulsory Gramdan and excessive rent ceilings
accepted.x: The 1961 ceiling law was weakened by benami transfers and exemptions.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementation loopholes rather than the formal purpose of the law.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1/1959, amended by 1/1970, primarily:
o: Barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
Created the National Land Reforms Council
Permitted unrestricted transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
Abolished all tenancy in the Andhra area
accepted.x: The Regulation barred the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.
accepted.tq: Apply the protective purpose of a tribal-area land-transfer regulation.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Land Reforms Bill passed by the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet under Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao provided for:
o: Transfer of all land to intermediaries
Ceiling on holdings and transfer of surplus land to the landless
accepted.x: The Bill imposed a ceiling on holdings and provided for distribution of surplus land to the landless.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operative measures of a reform bill from unrelated agrarian systems.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act, the ceiling for a family unit ranged from:
o: 15–35 acres wet and 40–60 acres dry land
5–15 acres wet and 20–40 acres dry land
20–40 acres wet and 50–75 acres dry land
10–27 acres wet and 35–54 acres dry land
accepted.x: The ceiling ranged from 10–27 acres of wet land or 35–54 acres of dry land, depending on land classification.
accepted.tq: Compare the two land categories and retain both numerical ranges.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The maximum area retainable under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act was:
accepted.x: The maximum retainable area was 54 acres of ‘K’ grade, the lowest-grade, land.
accepted.tq: Match the maximum ceiling with the specific land-grade classification.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Constitutional provisions were inserted or placed under protection by the First Amendment of 1951 in relation to land-reform laws?
o: Articles 44 and 51A and the Eighth Schedule
Articles 243A and 243B and the Eleventh Schedule
Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule
accepted.x: The First Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and placed laws in the Ninth Schedule to protect land reforms.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional shield with the amendment and its purpose.
accepted.sec: Land reform laws of AP and Hyderabad State → year and ministry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Council for Land Reforms, set up in 2008, was chaired by the:
accepted.x: The National Council for Land Reforms was set up in 2008 under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority associated with the institutional body.
accepted.sec: National Land Reforms Council - date, chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) began originally as the NLRMP in:
accepted.x: DILRMP began as the National Land Records Modernization Programme in 2008.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the programme’s original form and starting year from its later status.
accepted.sec: National Land Reforms Council - date, chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: DILRMP became a Central Sector Scheme in:
accepted.x: The programme became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016.
accepted.tq: Separate the launch year from the year of conversion into a Central Sector Scheme.
accepted.sec: National Land Reforms Council - date, chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with Phase 2 of DILRMP for 2016–26?
o: The Fifth and Sixth Schedules only
accepted.x: Phase 2 of DILRMP for 2016–26 covers ULPIN and NGDRS.
accepted.tq: Match the programme phase with its named components.
accepted.sec: National Land Reforms Council - date, chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru after the:
accepted.x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the National Integration Conference.
accepted.tq: Link the institution to its immediate constitutional-political origin.
accepted.sec: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate  [other exams]

accepted.s: The National Integration Conference that preceded the formation of the National Integration Council addressed which set of issues?
o: Inflation, unemployment, taxation and foreign trade
Land ceilings, tenancy, irrigation and consolidation
Disarmament, nuclear energy, space and cyber security
accepted.x: The conference considered communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism as threats to national integration.
accepted.tq: Recognise the thematic cluster associated with national integration policy.
accepted.sec: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a constitutional or institutional tool against regionalism?
accepted.x: The listed tools include the National Integration Council, Articles 44 and 51A, and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules. Article 32 exclusively is not included in that set.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated group of integration tools.
accepted.sec: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate  [other exams]

accepted.s: Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu that contributed to the two-language formula occurred in:
accepted.x: The relevant anti-Hindi agitations occurred in 1937, 1965 and 1986.
accepted.tq: Retain the three separate years and identify the complete chronological set.
accepted.sec: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 provided for the continued use of:
accepted.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 continued the use of English alongside the official language arrangements.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the statutory language provision from the languages involved in the agitations.
accepted.sec: National integration - NIC, origin, official language debate  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the phases of land reform in India:
1. Phase I covered 1947–70.
2. Phase II began in 1970 and continued thereafter.
3. The Kumarappa Committee of 1949 helped set the agenda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first phase covered 1947–70, the second began in 1970, and the Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the reform agenda.
accepted.tq: Combine periodisation with the committee associated with the reform agenda.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Which land-reform measure was regarded as the most successful and brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State?
accepted.x: Abolition of intermediaries was regarded as the most successful reform and brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.
accepted.tq: Match the reform measure with its recorded outcome.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Abolition of intermediaries covered approximately what share of cultivated area?
accepted.x: Abolition of intermediaries covered about 40 per cent of the cultivated area.
accepted.tq: Use the quantitative coverage figure to distinguish the reform’s scale.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Under tenancy reforms, rent was generally capped at what proportion of the produce?
accepted.x: Tenancy reforms generally capped rent at between one-fourth and one-sixth of the produce.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise range rather than reversing the numerator and denominator.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Tenancy reform was weakened in many areas by the practice of:
accepted.x: The practice of ‘voluntary surrenders’ enabled landlords to evade the protection intended by tenancy reforms.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementation device that undermined an otherwise protective reform.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an exception to the general weakness caused by ‘voluntary surrenders’ in tenancy reform?
accepted.x: Operation Barga, introduced in West Bengal in 1977, was an important exception to the general failure of tenancy reform.
accepted.tq: Find the exceptional programme among similarly named movements and operations.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: The two major rounds of land-ceiling legislation occurred during the:
accepted.x: Ceiling legislation was enacted in two major rounds, during the 1950s and the early 1970s.
accepted.tq: Place the two reform waves in their correct decades.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: From 1972, which unit was adopted for applying land ceilings?
accepted.x: The family was made the unit for applying land ceilings from 1972.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the legally relevant unit from administrative units such as village or district.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major method of evading land-ceiling laws?
accepted.x: Benami transfers were used to evade land-ceiling laws.
accepted.tq: Identify the evasion mechanism associated with ceiling legislation.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Land consolidation succeeded particularly in:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Land consolidation achieved notable success in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Match the reform with the geographical region where it succeeded.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Which State was the first to abolish zamindari in 1950?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh was the first State to abolish zamindari in 1950.
accepted.tq: Match the reform milestone with the pioneering State.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases

accepted.s: Raj Krishna classified land reforms into which four categories?
accepted.x: Raj Krishna classified land reforms as liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete four-part classification without substituting broader policy categories.
accepted.sec: Land reform phases
